Terms and model matrix of the fixed effects of a PGLMM

Source: R/pglmm-compat.R
pglmm-terms.Rd

terms() gives the terms object of the fixed effects of a model fitted by pglmm() or pglmm_compare(), and model.matrix() its design matrix of the fixed effects. They are used, with vcov() and fixef(), by packages such as emmeans, marginaleffects and effects, which work with pglmm() models (see Details).

Usage

# S3 method for class 'communityPGLMM'
terms(x, fixed.only = TRUE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'communityPGLMM'
model.matrix(object, ...)

Arguments

x, object

A model fitted by pglmm() or pglmm_compare().

fixed.only

Only TRUE (the fixed effects) is available.

...

Ignored.

Value

terms(): a terms object; model.matrix(): the design matrix of the fixed effects, with one row per observation used in the fit.

Details

Estimated marginal means and contrasts with emmeans::emmeans(), marginal effects and predictions with the marginaleffects package (e.g. marginaleffects::avg_slopes(), marginaleffects::predictions()), and effect plots with effects::Effect() and effects::allEffects() work with models fitted with bayes = FALSE. They use the fixed effects and their covariance matrix, with the random effects at zero, as for lme4 models; with marginaleffects, use re.form = NA for predictions without the random effects (the default, re.form = NULL, gives predictions conditional on the estimated random effects for the levels in the data). Degrees of freedom are asymptotic (z tests), as with glmmTMB().

marginaleffects accepts only the model classes it knows: until it knows those of phyr, set options(marginaleffects_model_classes = "communityPGLMM") before using it with pglmm() models.

Other packages that work with these models, through coef(), vcov(), terms(), model.matrix(), logLik(), nobs() and update(): Wald tests of the terms with car::Anova() and of linear hypotheses with car::linearHypothesis(); multiple comparisons with multcomp::glht(); likelihood ratio tests with lmtest::lrtest(); model selection and averaging with MuMIn::dredge() (with options(na.action = "na.fail")), MuMIn::model.sel() and MuMIn::model.avg(), which keep the random terms of the global model in all the submodels; and plots of predictions with ggeffects through emmeans (ggeffects::predict_response(fit, "x", margin = "marginalmeans") or ggeffects::ggemmeans()).
